ssrn-7371898.abstract: We examine the impact of regulatory fragmentation on firms' perceived riskiness. We find that firms' exposure to regulatory fragmentation is positively associated with optionsimplied perceived riskiness, while no such relationship is observed for regulatory intensity or regulatory pipeline. These effects are mainly driven by firms that are financially constrained, exhibit lower financial flexibility, incur higher overhead costs, and are less productive. We show that exogenous shocks that raise (lower) regulatory fragmentation lead to a substantial increase (decrease) in the perceived riskiness of firms that were subject to low (high) pre-shock regulatory fragmentation. We do not find such effects when there is an increase or decrease in the powers of a federal agency. We observe that firms' perceived riskiness increases further when they engage in lobbying and are exposed to greater regulatory fragmentation. With regard to real effect, we observe that firms' regulatory fragmentation positively affects the implied cost of equity. Overall, we identify regulatory fragmentation-related uncertainty as a novel determinant of option-implied risk, highlighting the role of firms' regulatory environment on risk management and option pricing.
ssrn-7371898.affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Udaipur, Indian Institute of Management Calcutta and Indian Institute of Management Calcutta

bullets: No one linked regulatory structure to option-implied risk
Split regulation into fragmentation, intensity, pipeline
Only fragmentation moves perceived riskiness
Effect concentrates in constrained, low-flexibility firms
en.data: US firms' regulatory fragmentation exposure matched to option-implied risk measures; sample window not stated in the abstract.
en.method: Regress firm-level regulatory fragmentation exposure on option-implied riskiness, with exogenous shocks to fragmentation and to federal agency power as identification.
en.one_liner: Regulatory fragmentation raises option-implied perceived risk of firms.
en.relevance_why: Score 2: option chains are standard, but the fragmentation measure must be built from federal regulatory text yourself, and no trading rule is given.
en.takeaway: Use fragmentation exposure as a screen for short-vol names or as a tilt in an implied-vol risk-premium model.

bullets: 규제 환경이 옵션 가격에 어떻게 스며드는지 몰랐다
규제 파편화·강도·예정 규제를 나눠 위험도와 연결했다
파편화만 위험도를 높였고 강도와 예정 규제는 무관했다
재무제약 기업일수록 효과가 크고 자본비용도 올랐다
ko.data: 미국 상장기업의 규제 문서 기반 파편화 지표와 옵션 내재 위험도를 결합했다. 표본 구간은 초록에 없다

ko.takeaway: 규제 파편화 지표를 옵션 매도 종목의 배제 필터나 내재변동성 리스크 프리미엄 조정 항으로 쓴다

ssrn-7372261.abstract: This study examines whether pre-expiration stock liquidity is associated with cross-sectional variation in price reactions to a potential increase in the supply of tradable shares, using IPO lockup expirations as pre-scheduled events. We construct a hand-collected dataset of lockup contracts from IPO disclosure documents for 522 IPO firms listed on the Mothers market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange between 2012 and 2021. Because lockup expiration dates are determined at the time of the IPO, this setting mitigates concerns that event timing is chosen in response to contemporaneous market conditions. We find a negative median cumulative abnormal return (CAR) around lockup expirations, and the magnitude of the reaction varies systematically with pre-expiration liquidity. Firms with higher pre-expiration turnover experience higher CAR, and this association remains significant in the joint specification. Higher Amihud illiquidity is associated with lower CAR in separate specifications, whereas wider bid-ask spreads show a marginally significant negative association; neither association remains statistically significant in the joint specification. The liquidity–CAR association is concentrated in the post-expiration window and is not statistically significant in the pre-expiration window, consistent with variation in post-expiration price reactions rather than pre-existing return trends. Overall, pre-expiration liquidity is associated with cross-sectional variation in post-expiration price reactions, with the most robust evidence coming from turnover.

bullets: Lockup expiration returns vary widely; what explains the spread?
Hand-collected lockup contracts plus a standard event study
Higher pre-expiration turnover means higher CAR; median CAR is negative
The liquidity effect shows up only after expiration, not before
en.data: 522 IPOs on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Mothers market, 2012-2021, with hand-collected lockup contracts.
en.method: Regress cumulative abnormal returns around expiration on turnover, Amihud illiquidity, and spread.
en.one_liner: Pre-expiration liquidity predicts price reactions at IPO lockup expirations.
en.relevance_why: Prices and volume are standard, but lockup dates require parsing Japanese IPO disclosures by hand, so the data pipeline is the real cost.
en.takeaway: Build a calendar of lockup expirations and short the low-turnover names into the date.

bullets: 락업 해제 충격의 횡단면 차이를 설명할 변수가 필요하다
IPO 공시에서 락업 계약을 직접 수집해 사건연구를 돌린다
회전율이 높을수록 누적초과수익(CAR)이 덜 하락한다
유동성 효과는 해제 이후 구간에만 나타난다

ko.method: 락업 해제일 기준 누적초과수익(CAR)을 유동성 지표에 회귀한다.

ssrn-7372321.abstract: This study analyses whether gold acts as a hedge or safe haven for the Indian stock market using long-run and crisis-specific return-based methods. Monthly data from 2008–2025 and daily data for the Global Financial Crisis, COVID-19, and the Russia–Ukraine war are used to estimate Pearson and Spearman correlations between gold and Nifty returns, with 60, 120, and 240-day windows. Results show moderate negative long-run correlation, indicating partial hedging, while safe-haven behaviour varies across crises and is strongest during the Russia–Ukraine war, highlighting time-varying diversification benefits.
ssrn-7372321.affiliations: Ranchi University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

bullets: Asks if gold's safe-haven role holds across different crises
Runs Pearson and Spearman over 60/120/240-day windows
Long-run correlation is moderately negative: partial hedge only
Safe-haven effect peaks during the Russia-Ukraine war
en.data: Monthly data 2008-2025, plus daily data for the GFC, COVID-19, and the Russia-Ukraine war.
en.method: Pearson and Spearman correlations between gold and Nifty returns on rolling windows.
en.one_liner: Tests whether gold hedges or shelters Indian equities, using return correlations.
en.relevance_why: Gold and Nifty prices are trivial to source, but the paper stops at correlations and gives no entry or exit rules.
en.takeaway: Justify tilting gold weight in an equity book by crisis regime, not as a constant hedge.

bullets: 금의 안전자산 역할이 위기마다 다른지 따진다

ko.method: 금과 니프티(Nifty) 수익률의 피어슨·스피어만 상관을 이동창으로 추정한다

ko.relevance_why: 금·니프티 가격은 구하기 쉽지만 상관 분석에 그쳐 매매 규칙이 없어 2점이다
ko.takeaway: 주식 포트폴리오의 금 비중을 위기 국면별로 조절하는 규칙의 근거로 삼는다

ssrn-7372430.abstract: This paper evaluates the extent to which standard quantitative sovereign default models exhibit equity return responses around default risk spikes comparable to the data. It finds that they largely do not. Hébert and Schreger (2017) employ a high-frequency event study around legal rulings and report a 10% increase in default risk causes a 6% decline in firms’ market value. A workhorse sovereign default model augmented with capital accumulation delivers only a 0.2% equity value drop. Three features account for the disconnect: the absence of private capital outflows and trade surpluses during default, the model’s counterfactual prediction of rising dividends, and the nominal depreciation embedded in the dollar-denominated index used in the data.

bullets: Models miss how default risk hits firm equity value
Author adds capital accumulation to a workhorse model
Data show -6% equity; the model gives only -0.2%
No capital outflows, rising dividends, dollar-index FX effect
en.data: Hébert and Schreger (2017) high-frequency event study around court rulings serves as the empirical benchmark.
en.method: A workhorse quantitative sovereign default model with capital accumulation, benchmarked against event-study estimates.
en.one_liner: Standard sovereign default models understate equity losses by 30x.
en.relevance_why: Pure macro model validation with no tradable rule; CDS and ruling dates are obtainable, but nothing here automates, so it scores 1.
en.takeaway: Strip the FX depreciation component before reading dollar-denominated EM equity moves around default events.

bullets: 국가부도 위험과 주가 반응의 연결이 모형에서 빠져 있다
자본축적을 넣은 표준 부도 모형과 실증치를 맞춰 본다
실증은 -6%인데 모형은 -0.2%만 내놓는다
자본유출·무역흑자 부재, 배당 상승, 환율 절하가 원인이다
ko.data: Hébert·Schreger(2017)의 법원 판결 기반 고빈도 이벤트 스터디 결과를 벤치마크로 쓴다.
ko.method: 자본축적을 추가한 표준 정량 국가부도 모형을 실증 이벤트 스터디 결과와 대조한다.
ko.one_liner: 국가부도 모형이 주식 반응을 30배 과소 추정한다고 밝힌다.

ssrn-7372430.title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Equity Return Consequences of Sovereign Default Risk

ssrn-7372499.abstract: The CAPM treats market beta as a sufficient statistic for priced aggregate risk. Yet expected returns compensate covariance with the stochastic discount factor, not covariance with the market itself. This distinction matters when some market fluctuations are orthogonal to the stochastic discount factor: they contribute to market volatility but not to the market risk premium. Market beta measures how much an asset covaries with the market, but not whether that covariance is generated by fluctuations relevant for marginal utility. I show that market beta combines exposure to priced and unpriced market variation. Under a priced-market spanning restriction, expected returns depend on priced beta, while unpriced beta has a zero structural price. Conventional beta therefore becomes an imperfect measure of compensated risk when assets load differently on the two components, generating CAPM pricing errors that increase with the difference in exposures. Empirically, priced and unpriced betas differ substantially across stocks. Consistent with the model, priced beta predicts average returns, unpriced beta carries little independent premium, and CAPM pricing errors increase with the exposure gap. Market beta's pricing performance therefore depends on what moves the market.

bullets: CAPM assumes market beta captures all priced risk
Returns pay for SDF covariance, not market covariance
Author decomposes beta under a spanning restriction
Priced beta predicts returns; unpriced beta earns nothing
en.data: Cross-section of individual stock returns; the abstract names no sample window.
en.method: An asset-pricing model that imposes a priced-market spanning restriction, giving unpriced beta a zero structural price.
en.one_liner: Splits market beta into a priced component and an unpriced one.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: return data is cheap and public, but you must build the SDF and spanning estimation yourself before any tradable rule exists.
en.takeaway: Hedge on priced beta instead of total beta, and trade the gap between the two betas as an alpha signal.

ssrn-7372719.abstract: Standard decentralized market making requires liquidity providers to commit capital before demand arrives. We study what replaces this capital when market design becomes more capital efficient. Comparing constant-product and oracle-based market makers, we show that flatter pricing rules reduce capital requirements by weakening inventory-based price adjustment and increasing reliance on external price information. Using on-chain data from tokenized real-world assets, we find that capital efficiency is strongest near target inventories and deteriorates with inventory imbalances. Reference-price updates redirect order flow, while stale executable prices predict trader selection and adverse markouts, with stronger trading responses when inventory sensitivity is lower. Capital efficiency therefore substitutes information for balance-sheet capital in liquidity provision.
ssrn-7372719.affiliations: LMU Munich School of Management and University of Regensburg - International Real Estate Business School (IREBS)

ssrn-7372719.title: Financing Liquidity with Capital or Information?

ssrn-7373058.abstract: "Time in the market beats timing the market" is among the most widely repeated maxims in investing, yet the investors who popularised it are almost all American and describe the American market. This paper asks whether the claim travels. Using MSCI country indices for six developed markets over 2000–2025, it measures how much an investor's final wealth depended on when their money entered, through two tests: the dispersion of outcomes across ten thousand randomly-timed passive investors, and the performance of two mechanical timing rules (a dip buyer and a hype chaser) against dollar-cost averaging. Both tests point to the same variable. Entry timing mattered far less than commonly assumed, and where it did matter it tracked a market's drift rather than its volatility: the US and Japan, with near-identical volatility, showed markedly different sensitivity to entry date. For deliberate timing the pattern reverses across markets — waiting for a 20% drawdown beat staying invested in Japan, the UK and Germany, but lost heavily in the high-drift US, where the dip buyer finished below all ten thousand randomly-timed investors. The correlation between a market's return and the penalty for timing it is strongly negative at −0.82. The mechanism is that time spent out of a rising market is a cost that scales with drift; the proverb is therefore best read not as a universal law but as a description of the exceptional US market that produced it.

bullets: The 'time in the market' maxim is US-derived; does it travel?

en.takeaway: Use trailing drift as a gate on whether a buy-the-dip entry rule is allowed in a given market.

ssrn-7374099.abstract: Redistribution capability is a structural component of adaptive liquidity systems, but its mathematical representation is not unique. A scalar quantity, reachable set, transition graph, transformation operator, or geometric object may preserve different information about the same underlying capability structure. This paper examines five principal mathematical realizations of redistribution capability: scalar, set-valued, graph-based, operator-based, and geometric. Relations between representations are formalized through an information preorder defined by deterministic recoverability. Mutual recoverability induces an equivalence relation, and the resulting equivalence classes form a partially ordered set under the induced information relation. The analysis distinguishes the underlying redistribution-capability structure Cσ(x) from a particular representation RA(σ, x) = ρA(Cσ(x)). For a specified class of dynamic contexts D, a dynamic response map ΨD is used to identify capability structures that are dynamically indistinguishable for the problem under consideration. The central result gives a necessary and sufficient factorization criterion for dynamic sufficiency. A representation ρ : C → Z is dynamically sufficient relative to D if and only if ΨD = Ψˆ︁ D ◦ ρ. Equivalently, every fiber of ρ must be contained within a single dynamic-equivalence class. This criterion separates generic information loss from dynamically relevant information loss. A representation may be non-injective and compress structural information while remaining dynamically sufficient, provided that it does not identify capability structures with different relevant dynamic responses. The resulting analysis provides a criterion for selecting mathematical realizations of redistribution capability relative to the system class, analytical task, and dynamic contexts under consideration. It does not assume a universal scalar realization or claim universal sufficiency of any single adaptive state representation.

bullets: No canonical representation exists for redistribution capability
Compares scalar, set, graph, operator, geometric forms
Proves dynamic sufficiency iff ΨD factors as Ψ̂D ∘ ρ
Non-injective representations can still be dynamically sufficient
en.data: Theory only
en.method: An information preorder from deterministic recoverability, plus a dynamic response map ΨD, orders representation equivalence classes.
en.one_liner: Formalizes five mathematical representations of redistribution capability and when each suffices.
en.relevance_why: Pure formalism with no signal, no numbers, no instruments — score 1; it uses no data at all, so sourcing is moot.
en.takeaway: Use it as a checklist for which liquidity-state information you can safely discard when compressing to features.

ssrn-7374119.abstract: This paper argues, and demonstrates constructively, that the natural mathematical object describing a stochastic process is an integro-differential equation rather than a partial differential equation. We begin from the elementary random walk, reconstructed as a sequence of additions of random variables, and show that the integral operator is present in the very first step of the derivation: it is not introduced as a technique, an approximation, or a generalization, but arises directly from the requirement that probability be conserved over all possible antecedents of a state. Passing to continuous time yields the master equation, which is local in time and nonlocal in space. We then reconstruct, step by step, the route by which the familiar partial differential equations of the field are obtained from it: the Kramers-Moyal expansion converts the integral operator into a differential operator of infinite order, and truncation at second order produces the Fokker-Planck equation and, in the financial setting, the Black-Scholes equation. We identify precisely the condition under which this truncation is exact, namely the vanishing of all jump moments above the second, which is equivalent to the continuity of sample paths. We then recall Pawula's theorem, which states that the expansion may terminate after the second term or must contain infinitely many terms, so that no intermediate truncation preserves the positivity of the probability density. This closes the space of possibilities: a stochastic process is described either by a second-order partial differential equation, at the price of assuming continuous paths, or by the full integral operator. We illustrate the theorem numerically for a compound Poisson process, exhibiting explicitly the negative density produced by third-order truncation. A second and independent source of integral operators is then developed: whenever a quantity is a function of random variables, its density is obtained through a generalized functional built on the Dirac delta, as introduced in The Boltzmann Equation in Finance [2]. Sums, products and ratios all generate integral operators, and contingent claims generate probability atoms that no diffusion operator can produce from smooth data. Allowing the population to act as its own environment renders the operator quadratic and yields the Boltzmann collision integral, within which diffusive spreading and concentration coexist, admitting non-trivial steady states unavailable to a translation-invariant Fokker-Planck equation. We close by distinguishing integration over state space, which produces jumps, from integration over time, which produces memory.

bullets: Black-Scholes is a truncation that presumes continuous sample paths
Derives the master equation, then rebuilds the PDE route from it
Pawula: truncating at third order breaks density positivity
Numerical compound Poisson case shows the negative density
en.data: Theory only, with one numerical compound Poisson illustration.
en.method: Master equation plus Kramers-Moyal expansion and Pawula's theorem, with Dirac-delta functionals generating integral operators for sums, products and ratios.
en.one_liner: Occhionero shows the native object of a stochastic process is an integro-differential equation, not a PDE.
en.relevance_why: Pure theory with no trading rules, but it attacks the diffusion assumption behind standard pricing, so it tells you what not to trust; data availability is a non-issue since none is needed, and all the cost sits in modelling.
en.takeaway: Reprice tail risk and contingent claims on jumpy assets with a jump integral term instead of a diffusion approximation.

ssrn-7374498.abstract: U.S. equity returns are known to be higher overnight, on Fridays, in January, around the turn of the month, and during macroeconomic announcement windows. We replicate 153 long-short factors and document the mirror image of these patterns: factor premia are systematically lower in exactly the same periods. On average, a factor loses 2.01 bps overnight but earns 5.45 bps intraday; it earns 5.77 bps on Mondays versus 1.24 bps on Fridays; and its returns are significantly lower in January, at the turn of the month, and around macroeconomic announcements. The reversed calendar effects persist out of sample and strengthen when news sentiment is elevated, consistent with sentiment-driven mispricing.
ssrn-7374498.affiliations: , Brandeis University and Brandeis University - International Business School

ssrn-7374498.title: Calendar Effects of Asset Pricing Factors

ssrn-7374679.abstract: Contractual lock-ups make previously restricted shares eligible to trade on dates fixed months in advance. This paper asks whether the trading response to a Hong Kong IPO cornerstone release depends on other releases reaching the market on the same session. Congestion is formed from a frozen pre-outcome census of 504 eligible release events; the focal sample contains 226 complete event windows for 2022-2025 listing cohorts. The primary equal-event specification models log(1 + event-session volume relative to the preceding-20-session mean), retains 11 zero-volume sessions, and controls for market turnover, issuer size, and pre-event liquidity. The crowded-session coefficient is 0.432 (event-session clustered p = 0.010) and its interaction with log(1 + release strength) is-0.683 (p = 0.018). Event-week clustering, wildcluster bootstrap inference, month-constrained calendar randomization, alternative same-session congestion measures, placebo dates, and joint omission of the most crowded sessions support the negative interaction. The result is scale-sensitive: asinh and positive-only log outcomes agree, but an untransformed volume-ratio model and a Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood share-flow model do not. Holm adjustment across volume, return, and volatility interactions gives p = 0.054; neither price nor range volatility is robust. The evidence therefore describes a typical-event transformed-volume pattern, strongest among smaller releases. It does not establish aggregate share-flow pressure, price dislocation, or a causal market-capacity mechanism.

bullets: Lock-up release dates are fixed months ahead and predictable
226 complete event windows, 2022-2025 HK listing cohorts
Crowded-session coefficient 0.432; interaction -0.683
Volume result survives; price and volatility effects do not
en.data: A frozen census of 504 eligible Hong Kong cornerstone release events, 2022-2025 listings, yielding 226 usable windows.
en.method: OLS on log(1 + event-session volume over the prior 20-session mean), with a crowded-session dummy interacted with log release strength.
en.one_liner: Tests whether same-day clustering of Hong Kong cornerstone lock-up expirations changes the volume response.
en.relevance_why: Scores 2 because cornerstone lock-up terms must be hand-extracted from HK prospectuses, and the paper reports no price or volatility edge.
en.takeaway: Build the release calendar in advance and shade down expected volume spikes for small releases landing on crowded sessions.

bullets: 락업 해제일은 몇 달 전에 확정돼 예측 가능하다

ssrn-7374679.title: Calendar Congestion and Trading Responses: Cornerstone Lock-up Expirations in Hong Kong IPOs

ssrn-7374758.abstract: Do repeated IPO intermediaries exhibit stable contracting histories, and do those histories improve genuine out-of-time prediction? We study 930 Hong Kong Main Board operating-company IPOs from 2018 through August 2026, 1,524 IPO-sponsor relationships, and 113 canonical sponsor entities. Sponsor histories use only strictly earlier listing dates. At the primary five-prior-deal threshold, the team adoption score has a raw AUC of 0.621 (year-stratified 95% bootstrap interval [0.571, 0.668]; within-year permutation p = 0.0004), while sponsor rankings persist across chronological halves (Spearman ρ = 0.610, p < 0.001). The controlled linear-probability coefficient is 0.390. Its p-value is 0.016 with leadsponsor clustered inference but 0.068 under a 4,999-draw wild-cluster bootstrap. Among single-sponsor IPOs the coefficient is 0.298 (clustered p = 0.081; wild-bootstrap p = 0.147), and omitting CICC reduces the full-team coefficient to 0.263 (p = 0.114). Expanding-window forecasts provide no stable incremental advantage: adding sponsor history changes pooled AUC from 0.691 to 0.682 (difference-0.009; bootstrap interval [-0.035, 0.017]). The difference is +0.030 in 2020-2023 but-0.040 in 2024-2026; the formal history-by-post-2024 interaction is imprecise (p = 0.660). Histories also do not predict release intensity or multi-tranche structure. Sponsor histories are persistent descriptors, but their association is dependence-sensitive and their predictive content becomes redundant as cornerstone adoption diffuses. The evidence is consistent with matching, networks, or routines rather than an exogenous sponsor effect or a portable forecasting advantage.

bullets: Tests whether repeat-sponsor histories forecast cornerstone use
Expanding-window prediction on 930 HK Main Board IPOs
Pooled AUC falls 0.691 to 0.682 when history is added
en.data: 930 Hong Kong Main Board operating-company IPOs, 1,524 IPO-sponsor pairs and 113 sponsors, 2018 through August 2026, split into 2020-2023 and 2024-2026 subperiods.
en.method: Builds a team adoption score from sponsors with 5+ strictly prior deals, then runs linear probability models with clustered and wild-cluster inference plus expanding-window AUC.
en.one_liner: Sponsor track records persist but add nothing to out-of-time forecasts of cornerstone adoption.
en.relevance_why: Score 2: sponsor-issuer relationship data must be hand-built from HK prospectuses, and the paper yields no tradable rule.
en.takeaway: Drop sponsor-history features from any cornerstone-participation model; they are redundant once adoption diffuses.

bullets: 스폰서 이력이 코너스톤 도입을 미리 맞추는지 검증

ko.takeaway: 코너스톤 참여 예측 모델을 짤 때 스폰서 이력 변수는 빼도 된다는 근거로 쓴다.

ssrn-7374758.title: Persistence Without Predictive Advantage: Sponsor Histories and Cornerstone Adoption in Hong Kong IPOs

ssrn-7375459.abstract: Retail investors reveal in public which stocks they are crowding into, and those stocks become more volatile the following week. Option prices, the market's forecast of that volatility, absorb only about half the signal. Measured from 86.7 million Reddit comments, attention keeps half its predictive power after the full surface is observed, and nonlinear readings do not close the gap. The absorbed half runs through the at-the-money term structure, not the smile, which attention nonetheless reshapes. The unabsorbed half improves volatility forecasts out of sample. Controlling for implied volatility does not control for what retail attention predicts.

bullets: Asks whether options already price retail crowding
Builds weekly attention from 86.7M Reddit comments
Half the predictive power survives the full IV surface
Absorbed half sits in ATM term structure, not the smile
en.data: 86.7 million Reddit comments matched to US equity option surfaces; the abstract names no sample window.
en.method: Regress realized volatility on Reddit attention while controlling for the full implied-vol surface, including nonlinear fits.
en.one_liner: Reddit attention predicts next-week volatility that option prices only half price in.
en.relevance_why: Score 3: the signal is clear and option data is standard, but you must scrape and clean 86.7M Reddit comments yourself.
en.takeaway: Add the unabsorbed attention residual to a vol forecast, then trade straddles or variance swaps against implied.

ssrn-7375459.title: Half the Signal: Retail Attention and the Price of Volatility

ssrn-7375498.abstract: This paper investigates whether unsupervised machine learning can identify economically meaningful regimes in the US equity market and whether such regimes provide genuine forecasting or investment value. Using a daily dataset of 3,823 observations spanning 18 October 2010 to 31 December 2025, sixteen standardized market, volatility, and macro-financial features are reduced via Principal Component Analysis (eight components explaining 92.1% of variance) and partitioned using K-Means clustering, validated against a Gaussian Mixture Model. The optimal solution, selected by silhouette score, identifies two statistically and economically distinct regimes, subsequently labelled Bull / Low-Risk (n = 3,201; 83.7% of observations) and Bear / High-Risk (n = 622; 16.3%). The regimes differ significantly across mean return, volatility, VIX level, momentum, and drawdown (Welch t-tests, all p < .001; Cohen's d up to 2.94), and exhibit strong persistence, with Bull-to-Bull and Bear-to-Bear transition probabilities of 96.5% and 81.8% respectively. A chronological, one-step-ahead out-of-sample forecasting exercise compares Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting classifiers against a naive persistence benchmark ("tomorrow's regime equals today's regime"). The persistence benchmark achieved the highest out-of-sample accuracy (93.55%), exceeding Random Forest (91.89%), Logistic Regression (89.80%), and Gradient Boosting (89.01%). This finding does not support the hypothesis that supervised machine learning provides superior next-day regime forecasting relative to a simple persistence rule. A regime-conditioned tactical investment strategy (fully invested in Bull, fully divested in Bear, signal lagged by one day, 10 basis point transaction costs) reduced maximum drawdown relative to buy-and-hold (-28.20% versus-33.92%) but underperformed on both compound annual growth rate (5.80% versus 12.68%) and Sharpe ratio (0.546 versus 0.780). Forward-return analysis indicates that returns following Bear/High-Risk observations were, on average, higher than returns following Bull/Low-Risk observations at 1-, 5-, and 20-day horizons, offering a plausible explanation for the strategy's return shortfall despite its lower drawdown. The study concludes that regime identification is statistically robust and economically interpretable, but that regime identification is not equivalent to reliable regime forecasting or to superior risk-adjusted investment performance. The paper's contribution lies in this explicit separation of unsupervised classification, supervised forecasting, and economic usefulness-three distinct questions that are frequently conflated in applied machine learning finance research. A supplementary robustness check (Section XI.J), which widens the feature set to twenty-nine variables by restoring the raw price, volume, and moving-average series the main specification deliberately excludes, produces a weaker four-regime solution and a severe train/test distribution shift that collapses out-of-sample forecasting performance-a negative result that, if anything, reinforces the original feature-exclusion rationale in Section IV.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Practitioners conflate regime labeling with regime forecasting
PCA cuts 16 features to 8 components (92.1%), K-Means splits 2 regimes
Naive persistence hits 93.55% vs Random Forest 91.89%
Regime timing cuts MDD to -28.20% but CAGR falls to 5.80%
en.data: 3,823 daily US equity observations, 18 Oct 2010 to 31 Dec 2025, with chronological one-step-ahead out-of-sample testing.
en.method: PCA plus K-Means (checked against a Gaussian Mixture Model), then Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting for next-day regime prediction.
en.one_liner: Clusters US equity regimes, then tests whether they forecast or pay.
en.relevance_why: Built entirely on public price, VIX, and macro data, so it replicates cheaply — but the regime strategy loses to buy-and-hold on CAGR (5.80% vs 12.68%) and Sharpe (0.546 vs 0.780).
en.takeaway: Use the regime label as a risk-dashboard or position-sizing input; skip the ML forecasters, since persistence beats them.

bullets: 국면 식별과 국면 예측을 흔히 같은 문제로 착각한다

ssrn-7375618.abstract: A fund can look greener without its manager shifting the portfolio toward greener firms. Independent measures agree that U.S. mutual fund carbon intensity fell by more than a third, yet portfolio reweighting explains only 1.2 percent. Most of the decline instead comes from changing issuer emissions, sales denominators, estimates, and coverage. These inputs reverse the institutional sector trend and reshuffle manager rankings. Attribution replaces two in five managers selected for a green mandate. The replacements subsequently trade greener than those they displace. Carbon scores measure portfolio exposure; attribution reveals who deserves credit for changing it.
ssrn-7375618.affiliations: and Queen's University - Smith School of Business

bullets: A fund looks greener without the manager buying greener firms
Splits carbon-score changes into reweighting versus input drift
U.S. mutual fund carbon intensity fell over one third
Attribution swaps out two in five green-mandate managers
en.data: U.S. mutual fund holdings plus independent carbon intensity measures; the abstract names no evaluation window.
en.method: Decomposes fund carbon intensity changes into portfolio reweighting and shifts in issuer emissions, sales denominators, estimates, and coverage.
en.one_liner: Only 1.2% of the drop in fund carbon scores comes from manager reweighting.
en.relevance_why: Original framing, but issuer emissions estimates and vendor coverage histories sit behind paid data, so replication is hard.
en.takeaway: Strip input drift out of carbon scores and rank managers or funds on the reweighting component alone.

ssrn-7375618.title: Who Gets Credit When Carbon Scores Fall?

ssrn-7375738.abstract: Passive inflows do not make firms issue equity indiscriminately. They redirect corporate share supply toward firms with real opportunities. I isolate those opportunities using federal purchasing growth in markets served by a firm's customers, which raises the firm's own sales. Index funds mostly get their shares from compensation and other transactions that bring the firm no money, and inflows raise no offerings on average. When a real opportunity arrives, supply shifts toward primary shares that raise cash. Firms already indexed issue far less against the same opportunity. Indexed ownership decides which opportunities get financed with new equity.

bullets: Unclear whether passive inflows expand corporate share supply
Instruments opportunity with federal purchases in customers' markets
Inflows raise no offerings on average across firms
Real opportunity shifts supply to cash-raising primary shares
en.data: U.S. firm equity issuance and index ownership linked to federal procurement data; the abstract names no sample window.
en.method: Instrumental-variables design using federal purchasing growth in a firm's customers' markets as an exogenous demand shock.
en.one_liner: Passive inflows redirect new share supply toward firms with real growth opportunities.
en.relevance_why: Corporate-finance evidence with no trading rule, and building customer-level federal procurement links is a heavy data lift.
en.takeaway: Screen for dilution risk by combining a firm's government-demand exposure with its index membership status.

ssrn-7375738.title: Passive Investing and the Supply of New Shares

ssrn-7375999.abstract: We study optimal execution with transient market impact when the instantaneous impact law is a weakly nonlinear deformation of the linear model, using rigorous perturbation theory. For completely monotone propagators with slippage, we show that the linear-impact optimizer has strictly positive trading rate, strengthening the nonnegativity result of Schied and Strehle (2021), and providing a necessary building block for rigorous perturbative expansions. We then consider a smooth deformation f (v; ε) of the instantaneous impact function, which reduces to linear impact at ε = 0, and develop a perturbative expansion in powers of ε. The expansion is asymptotic for smooth deformations and convergent for analytic deformations. The expansion is shown to be useful both for proving theorems, and also as a numerical tool. For propagators given by finite sums of exponentials, we prove in the weakly nonlinear regime the execution asymmetry that Curato, Gatheral, and Lillo (2017) observed numerically, and pointwise frontloading in the single exponential case. We also give a numerical example in which the square-root target is beyond the estimated radius of convergence, but the computed perturbation coefficients are still useful: ninth order truncation reduces the error of the linear baseline by a factor of about 43.

bullets: Linear impact models misprice real execution costs
Expands the optimizer in powers of a deformation parameter ε
Linear optimizer has strictly positive trading rate
Ninth-order truncation cuts linear-baseline error ~43x

en.takeaway: Bolt perturbative corrections onto a linear propagator schedule to frontload large parent orders more realistically.

ssrn-7376039.abstract: Using takeover announcements for unlisted targets as trigger events, we find that bidders disclose bids early if optimal to do so, and consummate bids promptly when the market reactions are favorable. We also find that bidders learn about deal-specific synergy from the market reactions, and learn more actively when the proprietary cost of early bid disclosure is high. These findings indicate that managers can obtain from market prices specific information about the real decision they face, and do so by voluntarily disclosing their planned action. The results further suggest that utilizing market feedback in timing bid consummation improves bidders’ future valuation, and market information creates value by filling a gap in managers’ private information. Our evidence points to obtaining market information as a potentially important rationale for voluntary disclosure.
ssrn-7376039.affiliations: Chulalongkorn University - Department of Banking & Finance and University of Strathclyde

en.method: Event study linking announcement timing, consummation speed, and announcement-window market reactions for unlisted-target bids.

en.relevance_why: Score 1: no tradable rule, and disclosure-timing data for private-target deals requires hand collection.
en.takeaway: Feed announcement-day return into a completion-probability model for merger arbitrage on private-target deals.

ssrn-7376118.abstract: Both practitioner commentary and the academic literature emphasize a negative relation between the volatility of returns and outcomes to constant leverage investment strategies such as leveraged ETFs (LETFs). I demonstrate that there is no hardwired negative relation in expectation. Rather, return serial covariances as captured by the return “Variance Ratio” are crucial; volatility increases average LETF returns in the presence of positive serial correlation and vice versa, and has no effect if returns are serially uncorrelated. In the presence of serial dependence, there are asymmetries in expected rebalancing costs across leveraged long vs. inverse strategies. However, return volatility widens the gap between expected and median compound LETF returns, because of increased skewness. The equations contained herein are extracted from a prior working paper titled "Returns to Constant Leverage Strategies: General Principles and Application to Leveraged Single-Stock ETFs."

bullets: Attacks the belief that volatility always drags on constant-leverage returns
Decomposes expected LETF returns via the return variance ratio
Positive serial correlation makes volatility raise average LETF returns
Zero serial correlation means zero effect, but skewness widens mean vs median
en.data: Theory only; equations are lifted from the author's earlier working paper on constant leverage strategies.
en.method: Analytical decomposition of expected compound returns for constant-leverage strategies into return serial covariances captured by the variance ratio.
en.one_liner: Volatility does not mechanically hurt leveraged ETFs; serial correlation decides the sign.
en.relevance_why: Variance ratios come from free daily prices, so data is trivial, but the paper sets no thresholds or holding rules — implementer's job.
en.takeaway: Gate leveraged ETF holding periods on the underlying's variance ratio, and size long vs inverse legs differently given asymmetric rebalancing costs.

bullets: 변동성이 레버리지 ETF 수익을 무조건 갉아먹는다는 통념을 겨냥한다

자기상관이 양수면 변동성이 평균 수익을 오히려 높이고 음수면 낮춘다
무상관이면 변동성 효과는 0이지만 왜도가 커져 평균과 중앙값 격차는 벌어진다
ko.data: 이론 연구다. 식은 저자의 이전 워킹페이퍼 'Returns to Constant Leverage Strategies'에서 가져왔다.
ko.method: 상수 레버리지 전략의 기대 복리수익을 수익률 시계열 공분산으로 전개해 분산비율과 연결한 해석적 도출이다.
ko.one_liner: 레버리지 ETF의 변동성 손실은 자동이 아니라 자기상관이 좌우한다
ko.relevance_why: 가격만 있으면 분산비율을 계산해 규칙으로 만들 수 있어 데이터 확보가 쉽지만 진입·청산 임계값은 직접 정해야 해서 4점이다.
ko.takeaway: 레버리지 ETF 보유 여부를 기초자산의 분산비율로 판정하고 롱과 인버스의 리밸런싱 비용 비대칭을 포지션 사이징에 반영한다.

ssrn-7376118.title: Volatility and Returns to Leveraged ETFs

ssrn-7376218.abstract: Institutional quantitative equity frameworks routinely mandate sector concentration limits or industry neutrality to eliminate uncompensated macroeconomic sector bets. While developedmarket long-short literature often supports neutralization, recent asset pricing theory [e.g., 6] demonstrates that long-only factor portfolios are systematically impaired by sector constraints because shorting decaying industries is disallowed. We provide an out-of-sample empirical investigation of this hypothesis in the Indian equity market using point-in-time National Stock Exchange (NSE) Nifty 500 constituent data across an 8-year historical sample (January 1, 2018 to February 26, 2026). Evaluating four parametric sector-cap regimes (C ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5}) and one sector-balanced selection regime against an unconstrained benchmark across 10 contiguous out-of-sample evaluation folds (1260 trading days / 5.0 trading years) under realistic transaction costs (42.34 bps round-trip friction including Securities Transaction Tax, stamp duty, exchange levies, and assumed 10 bps execution slippage), we document that all evaluated constrained configurations produce lower realized compound returns and Sharpe ratios than the unconstrained benchmark. An unconstrained 30-stock volatility-adjusted momentum strategy delivers an out-of-sample CAGR of 42.56% and a Sharpe ratio of 1.728. Capping sector allocations to 3 stocks compresses the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) from 0.169 to 0.084, but reduces CAGR to 33.97% (a-8.59pp annual drag) and Sharpe to 1.497 (unadjusted bootstrap p = 0.0204; Holm-adjusted bootstrap p = 0.1020; JKM p = 0.0281), with no improvement in maximum drawdown (-26.79% vs.-26.44%). We find evidence consistent with a factor dilution mechanism: sector caps exclude high-conviction momentum leaders in trending macro sectors, replacing them with lower-ranked securities from lagging industries (average selected momentum rank deteriorates from 15.5 to 48.2), which is positively associated with subsequent relative performance drag in Newey-West HAC predictive regressions (t = 2.41, p = 0.018).

bullets: Sector neutrality is standard practice but untested long-only
Five constrained regimes vs unconstrained on Nifty 500
Unconstrained CAGR 42.56% and Sharpe 1.728 beat all caps
Momentum rank of picks decays from 15.5 to 48.2 under caps
en.data: Point-in-time NSE Nifty 500 constituents, Jan 1 2018 to Feb 26 2026, 10 contiguous out-of-sample folds covering 1260 trading days.
en.method: A 30-stock volatility-adjusted momentum screen run under sector caps C∈{2,3,4,5} and a sector-balanced variant, benchmarked against no constraint.
en.one_liner: Sector caps cost a long-only momentum book 8.59pp of annual CAGR.
en.relevance_why: Rules are explicit and Nifty 500 prices plus sector tags are easy to source; +1 for refuting the sector-neutrality default, though caps trade at 42.34 bps round-trip friction that the author already models.
en.takeaway: Drop or loosen sector caps in long-only momentum, and price the drag explicitly before an institutional mandate imposes one.

ssrn-7376359.abstract: Grid trading is one of the most widely marketed algorithmic strategies on retail cryptocurrency exchanges, typically presented through screenshots of positive profitand-loss curves with little disclosure of deployed capital, holding period, or fee tier. This note examines whether grid trading generates an independent trading edge or whether its apparent profitability is better explained by market exposure, execution economics, and market-making infrastructure. We review three mechanically distinct implementations discussed in the recent literature-classical grid trading, Dynamic Grid Trading (DGT), and delta-neutral grid market making-and evaluate the evidentiary basis behind each. For classical grid trading, we rely on an existing analytical result showing zero expected profit under an explicitly stated symmetric random-walk model before costs. For Dynamic Grid Trading, we show that the reported outperformance over buy-and-hold is attributable in part to retained directional exposure over a period of substantial cumulative price appreciation, a point the source paper's own authors acknowledge. For delta-neutral grid market making, we identify an unresolved capital-accounting inconsistency and an incomplete fill model in the primary source, together with citation inconsistencies between its in-text attributions and its bibliography, and we supplement this with an original unit-economics illustration showing that the sign of a representative spot-leg cycle's economics flips from positive to negative when moving from the paper's assumed maker rebate to a standard retail maker fee. Taken together, the evidence indicates that grid trading is not a single strategy with a single source of return: as implementations move from a simple grid toward market-neutral market making, the economic source of any edge shifts away from the grid structure itself and toward fee schedules, execution quality, adverse-selection control, and market microstructure. We do not conduct an independent empirical replication of any of the three implementations; our contribution is a structured, source-verified synthesis of the existing evidence, a citation-consistency check on one of the primary sources, and a self-contained fee-sensitivity illustration.

bullets: Retail exchanges market grid bots with undisclosed capital and fee tiers
Reviews classical, Dynamic Grid Trading, and delta-neutral market making
Classical grid earns zero expected profit before costs under a symmetric random walk
A spot-leg cycle flips from profit to loss at a standard retail maker fee
en.data: Theory only — no independent empirical replication, just a self-contained unit-economics illustration.
en.method: Source-verified synthesis of three implementations, plus a citation check and an original fee-sensitivity calculation.
en.one_liner: Grid trading has no standalone edge; fees and microstructure explain the returns.
en.relevance_why: No tradeable signal to backtest, but exchange fee schedules and fills are trivially available and it debunks a heavily sold strategy — hence 3.
en.takeaway: Plug your own maker fee into a single grid cycle before funding any grid bot.

ssrn-7376938.abstract: Cloud compute expenditure in enterprise data engineering environments is rarely the result of insufficient capacity-it is the result of insufficient governance. This paper presents a framework for Databricks compute efficiency and cost optimization grounded in policy-driven, workload-aware infrastructure management, and evaluates that framework against a structured review of publications and technical reports spanning 2020-2026, of which 23 met a source-quality screen (Section 2) and were retained. The framework specifies five operating principles-zero idle compute tolerance, workloadspecific compute selection, policy-enforced cluster configuration, serverless-first architecture, and full cost attribution-mapped onto a medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) reference architecture with a five-level organizational maturity model. Literature synthesis indicates partial, uneven support: among the retained studies reporting direct cost or resource-utilization reductions, figures cluster in roughly the 18-30% range, alongside improved pipeline reliability and compliance posture. We further report a twoyear, single-organization deployment case study-an anonymized enterprise finance data platform-in which application of the framework reduced steady-state monthly compute billing for the affected workload by approximately 80% (from in excess of $150,000 to approximately $30,000 per month), a larger reduction than the literaturereported range, which we attribute primarily to an unusually unmanaged starting baseline. We discuss the framework's alignment with, and points of departure from, the reviewed literature, and identify independent, multi-organization validation as the primary direction for future work.

bullets: Overspend comes from weak governance, not thin capacity
Five rules: zero idle, serverless-first, full cost attribution
23 screened studies report 18-30% cost or utilization cuts
One finance platform cut billing from $150k to ~$30k a month
en.data: 23 publications and technical reports from 2020-2026, plus a two-year deployment at one anonymized enterprise finance data platform.
en.method: Five policy-driven compute principles mapped onto a Bronze/Silver/Gold medallion architecture and a five-level maturity model.
en.one_liner: A governance framework for cutting Databricks compute spend.
en.relevance_why: Scores 1 because it carries no tradable signal, and the supporting evidence is internal billing data nobody outside the firm can obtain.
en.takeaway: Borrow the cluster policies and cost-attribution rules to shrink the infra bill on a Databricks-hosted backtest or research pipeline.

ssrn-7376939.abstract: Writing unhedged options creates a liability-management problem in which the writer must determine both where contractual losses attach and how finite capital is distributed across those exposures. We develop a static terminal framework for European cash-settled written options that jointly represents lower put liabilities, upper call liabilities, and their capital allocations. More specifically, the model separates observed premium income from physical claim risk, expresses each liability per unit of declared capital, and evaluates the portfolio through expected underwriting surplus and the raw second moment of aggregate claims. Under a multivariate lognormal terminal law, we obtain analytical claim moments, characterize conditional capital allocation and local strike conditions, and show that Gaussian dependence affects same-tail and opposite-tail claim accumulation in different directions. We then apply the framework to archived Deribit crypto-option formations using point-in-time contract screens, fixed-moneyness benchmarks, and paired dependence-aware uncertainty. We find positive average gross-surplus differences for the staged policies in the completed samples, although the associated dispersion and tail effects are not uniform and a realized uncovered-call claim exceeds its finite capital proxy. Thus, the empirical evidence supports the use of the framework as a solvency-aware underwriting and diagnostic architecture, but it does not establish calibrated tail probabilities, executable net profitability, or broker-margin survival.
categories: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis
journals: Quantitative Methods in Investing & Financial Statement Analysis

bullets: Unhedged writers must set loss attachment points and split capital
Model states put and call liabilities per unit of declared capital
Closed-form claim moments under a multivariate lognormal terminal law
Deribit tests show positive mean gross-surplus gaps, uneven tails
en.data: Archived Deribit crypto-option formations, screened point-in-time against fixed-moneyness benchmarks; the window is not stated.
en.method: A static terminal model separating premium income from claim risk, with analytical moments and conditional capital allocation under multivariate lognormal terminal prices.
en.one_liner: Recasts unhedged European option writing as an insurance underwriting problem with finite capital.
en.relevance_why: Deribit chains are public and easy to source, but the paper gives no entry or exit rules and explicitly disclaims executable net profitability, so it caps at 3.
en.takeaway: Bolt it on as a solvency diagnostic for a short-option book: how much capital each tail can consume and when two tails fire together.

bullets: 무헤지 매도자는 손실 부착점과 자본 배분을 같이 정해야 한다
풋·콜 부채를 선언 자본 단위로 표준화해 잉여와 2차 적률을 계산한다
다변량 로그정규 가정에서 청구 적률의 해석해를 구했다
Deribit 데이터에서 총잉여 차이는 평균 양수지만 꼬리는 고르지 않다
ko.data: 아카이브된 Deribit 암호화폐 옵션 조합을 시점 고정 계약 스크린과 고정 머니니스 벤치마크로 검증했다. 구간은 밝히지 않았다.
ko.method: 다변량 로그정규(multivariate lognormal) 만기 분포에서 풋·콜 청구액의 적률을 닫힌 형태로 풀고 조건부 자본 배분과 국소 행사가 조건을 유도한다.
ko.one_liner: 무헤지 옵션 매도를 보험 인수 문제로 다시 짠 정적 모형이다.
ko.relevance_why: Deribit 옵션 체인은 공개 데이터라 확보가 어렵지 않지만 진입·청산 규칙이 없고 저자도 실행 가능한 순수익성은 입증하지 못했다고 못 박아 3점이다.
ko.takeaway: 옵션 매도 북의 자본 소진과 동시 청구 위험을 사전 점검하는 리스크 진단 층으로 붙일 만하다.

ssrn-7376939.title: Theory of European Option Underwriting Portfolios

ssrn-7379518.abstract: We develop a simple and replicable five-variable model that identifies index-based investors with 98% accuracy. Our analysis shows that index ownership grew from 3.0% of global market capitalization in 2004 to 16.9% by 2023, driven by growth in explicit indexing. By the end of 2023, index-based investors own 10 percent or more of 5,300 firms globally. In the U.S., mid-caps have more index ownership than large-caps. In Asia and Europe, index ownership increases with firm size, and only the largest firms experience significant index ownership. Differences in market capitalization and free float help explain regional variations in index ownership.
ssrn-7379518.affiliations: Stockholm School of Economics, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) and Stockholm School of Economics - Stockholm School of Economics - Swedish House of Finance, Students

bullets: No replicable way existed to tag index investors
Five-variable model classifies them with 98% accuracy
Index ownership rose from 3.0% to 16.9% of global cap
US mid-caps carry more index ownership than large-caps
en.data: Global equity holdings 2004-2023, plus market cap and free float by region.
en.method: A simple five-variable classifier flags which investors are index-based.
en.one_liner: The authors measure index-investor ownership of firms worldwide from 2004 to 2023.
en.relevance_why: Descriptive study with no trading rule, and firm-level holdings data sits behind expensive vendor feeds.
en.takeaway: Attach per-firm index ownership as a crowding feature to anticipate rebalance-driven price pressure.

bullets: 인덱스 보유 지분을 종목별로 재는 방법이 없었다
5개 변수 모델로 인덱스 투자자를 98% 정확도로 분류
미국은 중형주가 대형주보다 인덱스 지분이 높다
ko.data: 2004~2023년 글로벌 주식 보유 지분 데이터, 지역별 시총·유동주식 비중 포함.
ko.method: 다섯 변수만 쓰는 단순 분류 모델로 투자자가 인덱스형인지 판별한다.
ko.one_liner: 인덱스 투자자 지분을 5개 변수로 식별해 전 세계 20년 추이를 집계했다.
ko.relevance_why: 매매 규칙이 없는 실태 분석이고 종목 단위 보유 지분 데이터가 유료 기관용이라 재현 문턱이 높다.
ko.takeaway: 종목별 인덱스 지분율을 유동성·수급 팩터로 붙여 리밸런싱 시기의 가격 압력을 걸러낸다.

ssrn-7379518.title: The Global Rise of Index-Based Ownership of Firms

ssrn-7379989.abstract: The relevant empirical question about momentum in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) is not whether it works, but whether simple operational rules can extract value from it. We show that pure momentum over a broad ETF universe creates no value: replicated across 3,215 investable U.S. ETFs, it delivers Sharpe ratios between −0.17 and +0.22 with drawdowns of 69% to 82%, systematically below passive investing. Yet three layers of rules available to any investor fully reverse that conclusion. We evaluate the 2001–2026 period (1,289 weeks) across the investable universe, charging a 20-basis-point transaction cost per side at every stage of the analysis. On top of replicating classic cross-sectional momentum, we add technical entry signals, a multi-horizon momentum ranking with mandatory diversification across super-categories within an eight-position portfolio, and an expanded family of 144 dynamic stop-loss and take-profit exit rules, all under an asymmetric rebalancing regime of biweekly purchases and weekly exit monitoring. The complete strategy delivers a Sharpe ratio above 1.3 and a maximum drawdown of −7%, beating passive investing by close to a full Sharpe point; the alpha concentrates in tail-risk reduction and is impaired only during the high-implied-volatility regime. The central implication for researchers and practitioners is that the value comes not from the technical signal but from the operational management layer that surrounds it.
ssrn-7379989.affiliations: Universidad Diego Portales and Universidad Diego Portales

bullets: Pure ETF momentum loses to passive, so what fixes it?
Add technical entries, multi-horizon ranks, 144 exit rules
Sharpe rises above 1.3; max drawdown shrinks to -7%
Alpha comes from tail-risk cuts, not the signal
en.data: 3,215 investable U.S. ETFs over 2001-2026, 1,289 weeks, charging 20 bps per side at every stage.
en.method: Classic cross-sectional momentum plus technical entry filters, an eight-position multi-horizon rank with forced super-category diversification, and 144 dynamic stop-loss/take-profit exits under biweekly buys and weekly exit checks.
en.one_liner: ETF momentum pays only when operational rules wrap it.
en.relevance_why: Rules, universe and cadence are fully specified on public ETF prices, and it also refutes plain ETF momentum, whose Sharpe runs -0.17 to +0.22 with 69-82% drawdowns.
en.takeaway: Bolt the exit-rule and diversification layer onto an existing momentum sleeve to cut drawdowns.

bullets: 순수 모멘텀만으로는 패시브보다 못하다는 문제
기술적 진입, 다기간 랭킹, 손절·익절 144종을 얹었다
샤프 1.3 초과, 최대낙폭 -7%로 개선됐다
알파는 신호가 아니라 꼬리위험 축소에서 나온다
ko.data: 미국 상장 투자가능 ETF 3,215종을 2001~2026년 1,289주 구간에서 검증했고 편도 20bp 거래비용을 전 단계에 물렸다.
ko.method: 고전 횡단면 모멘텀에 기술적 진입 신호, 슈퍼카테고리 분산을 강제한 8종목 다기간 랭킹, 손절·익절 규칙 144종을 겹쳐 쌓았다.
ko.one_liner: ETF 모멘텀은 운용 규칙을 씌워야 돈이 된다.
ko.relevance_why: 규칙과 리밸런싱 주기가 다 적혀 있고 ETF 가격은 누구나 구하므로 그대로 백테스트할 수 있다. 순수 모멘텀이 무가치하다는 반증도 더했다.
ko.takeaway: 모멘텀 랭킹 위에 격주 매수·주간 청산 점검과 동적 손절·익절을 얹어 낙폭을 줄이는 운용 계층으로 쓴다.

ssrn-7379989.title: Momentum Strategies in ETFs under Simple Operational Rules: Economic Value and Conditional Predictability

ssrn-7379990.abstract: The information investors acquire in financial markets has various forms. We refer to range information as information about the upper and lower bound which the payoff of an asset may reach in the future. This study develops rational expectation models to explore the market impacts of investors' asymmetrical acquisition of range information. Uninformed traders are inherently unable to directly obtain the private signal held by informed traders. Our model shows that when range information is released to investors asymmetrically, uninformed traders who can only obtain rougher range information will not trade assets under the max-min ambiguity aversion criterion. Investors' asymmetrical acquisition of range information can cause that market liquidity and the sensitivity of market price to private signal vary continuously with the signal and noise trading volume. Our model also reveals that investors' asymmetrical acquisition of range information can decrease market liquidity and increase the sensitivity of price under some conditions and we also specify these conditions.
ssrn-7379990.affiliations: Shandong Normal University, Shandong University of Finance and Economics and Shandong University of Finance and Economics

bullets: Prior asymmetry models focus on signal precision, not bounds
Defines range information: the payoff's upper and lower limits
Solves a rational expectations equilibrium with ambiguity aversion
Traders holding only coarse bounds stop trading entirely
en.data: Theory only
en.method: A rational expectations equilibrium where uninformed traders optimize under a max-min ambiguity aversion criterion.
en.one_liner: Models how asymmetric access to an asset's payoff bounds reshapes liquidity and price sensitivity.
en.relevance_why: Pure theory with zero trading rules, and the model's range information has no observable counterpart in market data.
en.takeaway: A lens for reading why spreads widen in names with severe information asymmetry — no signal to trade.

bullets: 기존 정보 비대칭 모형은 신호의 정확도만 다뤘다
가치의 상한·하한이라는 '범위 정보'를 새로 정의했다
합리적 기대(rational expectation) 균형 모형으로 분석했다
거친 범위 정보만 가진 투자자는 아예 거래를 접는다
ko.data: 이론 연구
ko.method: max-min 모호성 회피(ambiguity aversion) 기준을 넣은 합리적 기대 균형 모형을 세워 균형 가격과 거래량을 푼다
ko.one_liner: 자산 가치 상하한 정보의 비대칭이 유동성과 가격 민감도를 어떻게 바꾸는지 이론으로 푼다
ko.relevance_why: 거래 규칙이 하나도 없는 순수 이론이고 모형 속 '범위 정보'는 시장 데이터로 관측할 방법조차 없어 1점을 줬다
ko.takeaway: 정보 비대칭이 큰 종목에서 유동성 공급자의 호가 스프레드가 왜 벌어지는지 해석하는 틀 정도로만 쓸 만하다

ssrn-7379990.title: The asymmetrical acquisition of information about the range of asset value in market

ssrn-7381658.abstract: The third derivative of bond price with respect to yield, the analogue of gamma for fixed income, has been derived before but treated as a deterministic curiosity of marginal importance. This paper advances and tests a single hypothesis: that this third-order term is economically material during macroeconomic crises, with a contribution to expected price change governed jointly by maturity, the size of the yield move, and the asymmetry of the yield-change distribution. We treat the yield change as a random variable and establish a two-stage existence theorem. Under a normal distribution with non-zero drift the term acts through a puredrift channel and a drift-variance channel; the Normal-Inverse Gaussian extension adds exactly one further term, a pure-skewness channel proportional to the third cumulant that vanishes under any symmetric distribution. Empirically, across the 1973-74 oil shock, the 2000-02 dot-com deflation, the 2007-09 global financial crisis, and the COVID-19 2020 shock measured with Adrian-Crump-Moench data, the third-order sensitivity scales cubically with maturity (a thirty-year to two-year ratio of roughly 525 to 690 across the three historical crises, and about 1380 in the low-yield COVID window), the gamma-to-convexity ratio rises from 1.9 percent at two years to 17.5 percent at thirty years at crisis-scale moves and holds at a stable 0.76 of the Brooks-Livingston convexity-to-duration ratio, and the skewness channel reaches 48 to 86 percent of the drift channels for thirty-year bonds, offsetting most of the normal-distribution gamma contribution in the dot-com episode. The skewness condition itself is confirmed decisively in daily settlement data for five CME Treasury futures contracts, with a pooled statistic of χ²(3) = 73.4 and significant within-window skewness in the dot-com episode, while the global financial crisis window is fattailed rather than skewed; the shorter monthly windows lack the power to reject symmetry on their own. The third-order term is negligible in the small, symmetric setting examined by earlier work and material in the large, directional, asymmetric moves that characterize crises.

bullets: Prior work dismissed the third-order term as a deterministic curiosity
Treats yield change as random, proves a two-stage existence theorem
Gamma-to-convexity climbs from 1.9% at 2y to 17.5% at 30y
en.data: Adrian-Crump-Moench yields across the 1973-74 oil shock, 2000-02 dot-com, 2007-09 GFC and 2020 COVID windows, with skewness tested on daily settlements for five CME Treasury futures (pooled χ²(3) = 73.4).
en.method: Decomposes the third-order term into pure-drift and drift-variance channels under a normal yield distribution, plus one pure-skewness channel under a Normal-Inverse Gaussian.
en.one_liner: The third derivative of bond price to yield matters in crises, not in calm markets.
en.relevance_why: ACM curves and CME settlements are free and public, so replication is cheap, but this is a risk-pricing correction rather than an entry/exit rule, so it needs real strategy design on top.
en.takeaway: Add the third-order term to P&L approximations for long-maturity crisis positions and tilt duration hedges by the sign of yield skewness.

bullets: 3차 항은 그동안 무시해도 되는 상수 취급을 받았다
수익률 변화를 확률변수로 놓고 2단계 존재정리를 세웠다
30년물에서 감마/컨벡시티 비율이 17.5%까지 올라간다
ko.data: Adrian-Crump-Moench 수익률 곡선으로 1973-74 오일쇼크, 2000-02 닷컴 붕괴, 2007-09 금융위기, 2020 코로나 국면을 다뤘고 CME 국채선물 5종 일별 정산가로 왜도를 검정했다
ko.method: 수익률 변화에 정규분포와 정규-역가우시안(Normal-Inverse Gaussian)을 각각 적용해 순수 드리프트, 드리프트-분산, 순수 왜도 세 채널로 3차 항을 분해한다
ko.one_liner: 채권 가격의 3차 미분항이 위기 국면에서 실제로 돈이 된다는 걸 검증했다
ko.relevance_why: ACM 곡선과 CME 선물 정산가 모두 공개 데이터라 재현은 쉽지만 매수·매도 규칙이 아니라 리스크 계산식이라 전략으로 만들려면 설계가 더 필요해 3점이다
ko.takeaway: 위기 국면 장기물 포지션의 손익 근사에 3차 항을 넣고 왜도 부호에 따라 듀레이션 헤지 비율을 조정한다

ssrn-7381658.title: The Third Derivative of Bond Prices: Skewness, Drift, and Expected Returns in Crisis Regimes

ssrn-7381810.abstract: Most machine learning trading strategies are judged by their annualized return, that is, the average gain or loss over a year. That figure says nothing about the speed of the price movements that produce it. We take a machine learning portfolio built for Bursa Malaysia, rebuild its daily returns exactly from its stored holdings over 2022 to 2025, and split those returns into layers by how long each movement lasts, from two-day fluctuations to trends beyond 128 trading days. We then compare every layer with five Malaysian benchmark indices and four global market forces. The results show two distinct parts. At horizons beyond six months, it simply rides the Malaysian market. At the one-quarter to half-year horizon it moves almost independently of the large-cap index, with a beta of 0.09, and this independent layer is unchanged after trading costs. Its co-movement with the market is confined to crisis episodes, and no global force tracks it.
ssrn-7381810.affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN
authors: Ahmad Shauqi bin Haji Mohamad Zubir
Wan Nurul Nisrin binti Wan Mohd Zamani

bullets: Annualized return hides which horizon actually earns the money
Rebuilds daily returns from holdings, layers them 2 to 128+ days
Beyond six months the strategy just rides the Malaysian market
Quarter-to-half-year layer: beta 0.09, survives trading costs
en.data: One Bursa Malaysia ML portfolio's holdings, 2022-2025, plus 5 Malaysian benchmark indices and 4 global market factors.
en.method: Rebuild daily returns from stored holdings, decompose into duration layers, regress each layer on 5 Malaysian indices and 4 global forces.
en.one_liner: Splits an ML portfolio's returns by movement duration to locate its alpha.
en.relevance_why: A post-hoc attribution method, not a trading rule, and the specific ML portfolio's holdings are proprietary to the authors, though the technique applies to any strategy whose daily returns you own.
en.takeaway: Use it as a diagnostic: split your own strategy's returns by horizon to separate beta-riding layers from genuinely independent ones.

bullets: 연율 수익률만으로는 알파가 어느 속도에서 나오는지 모른다
일별 수익을 2일~128일 이상 시간 층으로 분해했다
6개월 초과 구간은 그냥 시장 추종이었다
분기~반기 층은 대형주 지수 베타 0.09로 거의 독립이다
ko.data: 2022~2025년 부르사 말레이시아 ML 포트폴리오의 보유 기록과 말레이시아 지수 5개, 글로벌 시장 요인 4개
ko.method: 저장된 보유 종목에서 일별 수익을 복원한 뒤 지속 기간별 층으로 나누고 층마다 벤치마크 5개와 글로벌 요인 4개에 회귀했다
ko.one_liner: ML 포트폴리오 수익을 보유 기간별로 쪼개 알파의 출처를 찾았다
ko.relevance_why: 매매 규칙이 아니라 사후 분해 기법이라 전략화하려면 설계가 더 필요하고, 대상 ML 포트폴리오의 보유 기록은 저자 고유 자산이라 외부에서 못 구한다
ko.takeaway: 기존 전략 수익을 기간별로 쪼개 시장 추종 층과 진짜 독립 층을 갈라내는 성과 진단 도구로 쓴다

ssrn-7381810.title: Does machine learning beat the market by trading fast or by waiting? Evidence from Bursa Malaysia

ssrn-7382219.abstract: The United States has increasingly leveraged the Entity List as a key instrument within its export control regime. While existing studies primarily examine the political motivations and macroeconomic consequences of these measures, we extend the literature by empirically investigating the link between U.S. Entity List targeting Chinese entities and stock price crash risk of affected Chinese firms. Utilizing a panel dataset of Chinese listed companies spanning 2012–2023, we find a positive association between U.S. Entity List sanctions and stock price crash risk. The identified channels include increased overseas supply vulnerability, weakened inventory turnover efficiency, and increased managerial risk narrative suppression. U.S. Entity List sanctions particularly increase stock price crash risk in firms with greater internal control deficiencies, lower analyst coverage, more negative investor sentiment, and longer financial disclosure delays. These findings identify targeted export control policy shocks as a novel driver of stock price crash risk, underscoring the need for policymakers to anchor market expectations and for listed firms to develop sanction-resilient governance and risk management that foster the sustainable development of financial markets.
ssrn-7382219.affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan University and Sichuan University

bullets: Sanctions research covers politics and macro, not firm crash risk
Panel regressions on Chinese listed firms, 2012-2023
Listed firms show higher stock price crash risk
Effect concentrates in weak internal controls, thin analyst coverage
en.data: Panel of Chinese listed companies, 2012-2023.
en.method: Panel regressions link Entity List designation to crash risk, with overseas supply vulnerability, inventory turnover, and suppressed managerial risk narratives as channels.
en.one_liner: U.S. Entity List listing raises crash risk in the targeted Chinese firms' stocks.
en.relevance_why: Score 1: a policy-shock regression with no trading rule; the BIS list is public, but mapping entities to listed tickers and building internal-control and sentiment proxies is heavy manual work.
en.takeaway: Use designation dates as an event-driven risk filter to cut tail exposure on individual China A-share names.

bullets: 제재 연구는 정치·거시에 쏠려 기업 주가 위험은 비었다
2012~2023년 중국 상장사 패널로 등재 효과를 추정한다
등재 기업의 주가 급락 위험이 유의하게 커진다
내부통제 부실, 낮은 애널리스트 커버리지에서 효과가 세다

ko.one_liner: 미국 제재 명단 등재가 중국 상장사 주가 급락 위험을 높인다

ko.takeaway: 제재 명단 등재일을 이벤트로 삼아 중국 A주 개별 종목의 꼬리위험 익스포저를 줄이는 리스크 필터로 쓸 만하다

ssrn-7382219.title: U.S. Entity List sanctions and corporate stock price crash risk: evidence from China

ssrn-7382221.abstract: Institutional site visits enable investors to obtain incremental information beyond routine public disclosures and engage directly with corporate managers. This study posits that site visits may facilitate the early transmission of event-related information to the market, thereby contributing to price reactions before major corporate announcements. Using mandatory disclosures of site visits in China, this study finds that firms receiving site visits experience higher cumulative abnormal returns before profit distribution announcements, consistent with the view that site visits transmit information to the market before formal disclosure. The incremental pricing effect of site visits, however, weakens when event signals become stronger. Investor attention further facilitates the pricing of site-visit-related information, whereas different sources of information complexity either strengthen this pricing role in high-signal payout events or weaken the general transmission of site-visit information. Further trading evidence shows that major shareholders and executives are more likely to reduce their holdings when their trading operations are preceded by high-signal payout events with prior site visits, and that mutual funds affiliated with the corresponding site-visit institutions exhibit staged holding adjustments around these events. Overall, the evidence suggests that site visits provide an observable channel through which incremental information enters prices before formal disclosure, although this pricing role varies with event signal strength and information-processing conditions.

bullets: Targets how private info leaks into prices pre-announcement

ssrn-7382222.abstract: Frequent geopolitical shocks and swings in global energy prices have strengthened cross-market connectedness and tail risk spillover among energy, equity and foreign exchange markets, which suggests that conventional static portfolio optimization may fail to adapt to intricate market conditions. This paper establishes a time-varying bi-objective portfolio optimization framework built upon the dynamic R-Vine Copula model. Empirical evidence points to notable lower-tail dependence across the three markets; the magnitude of risk spillovers appears to surge amid crisis episodes such as geopolitical clashes and global monetary tightening cycles. By embedding dynamic risk contagion channels into portfolio decision rules, the proposed model allows for adaptive weight rebalancing that seeks a trade-off between return maximization and CVaR minimization. Based on the evaluation metrics adopted in this research, the dynamic optimization strategy tends to deliver better performance relative to static specifications and equal-weighted benchmark portfolios in respect of risk-adjusted returns and downside risk containment. The present work may offer viable methodological references for constructing cross-market dynamic portfolios, and its findings could provide tentative practical insights for investors conducting multi-asset allocation and managing cross-market systemic risks.
ssrn-7382222.affiliations: Southwest Jiaotong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN , Southwest Petroleum University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

ssrn-7383518.abstract: Financial regulators promote open data to dismantle monopolies and improve transparency. Yet financial data feeds bundle two distinct objects: information about fundamentals and about liquidity demand. In a strategic-trading model with an upstream data market, competition among data vendors broadens fundamental access and sharpens price discovery, but also induces them to disseminate order-flow signals. These reveal no fundamentals but make liquidity demand predictable, raising market makers' price impact. Hence an open-data paradox: competition can make prices more informative yet markets less liquid. We characterize an information-design remedy, selective openness: broad fundamental access with restricted order-flow data.
ssrn-7383518.affiliations: , and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST)

bullets: Regulators push open data but ignore the liquidity side

en.takeaway: Use it to argue which way execution-cost assumptions should move if data-access rules change.

ssrn-7388478.abstract: Business Development Companies (BDCs) combine periodic reporting of illiquid private credit with continuously traded equity, providing a unique setting to evaluate private credit performance. During periods of credit stress, performance drops and stock-to-NAV discounts widen sharply as stock prices fall faster than reported NAVs. Market discounts and pre-announcement stock returns predict subsequent NAV markdowns and weaker profitability, although their predictive power is limited for larger BDCs and those with more diversified portfolios. Crucially, market metrics have limited ability to anticipate discrete distress events such as non-accruals and payment-in-kind (PIK) amendments. We find that quarterly NAV announcements contain significant, value-relevant incremental information that results in immediate stock price reactions.
ssrn-7388478.affiliations: Georgetown University - Robert Emmett McDonough School of Business , Ohio State University (OSU) - Department of Finance and

bullets: Private credit reports quarterly, so losses surface late

en.data: BDC quarterly NAV announcements matched to daily equity prices, spanning credit stress periods.
en.method: Regress subsequent NAV markdowns and profitability on stock-to-NAV discounts and pre-announcement returns; measure announcement-day price reactions.
en.one_liner: BDC stock-to-NAV discounts forecast private credit markdowns.
en.relevance_why: Prices and NAVs are public and easy to pull, but the paper gives features, not entry and exit rules.
en.takeaway: Use the BDC discount as an early-warning gauge on private credit exposure, discounting it for large, diversified BDCs.
